title: ConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone.lean

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Constrained monotone variational inequality: find xstar ∈ X satisfying ⟨F(xstar), w − xstar⟩ ≥ 0 for every w ∈ X. X is convex; F is continuous and globally monotone. No objective function, strong monotonicity, or saddle representation is assumed.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Oracle 1 returns an exact Euclidean metric projection P(z) onto X, characterized by P(z) ∈ X and ⟨z − P(z), w − P(z)⟩ ≤ 0 for every w ∈ X. Operator evaluations and projections have separate fixed call budgets.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone.lean: spec.admissible, second conjunct; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Oracle 0 returns the exact operator value F(x) at any ambient-space query x. Answers are independent of the call index and seed; F need not be a gradient.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: L0 > 0 and L1 ≥ 0. For every x, y and M, a bound ‖F(x + θ(y − x))‖ ≤ M throughout θ ∈ [0,1] implies ‖F(x) − F(y)‖ ≤ (L0 + L1 M)‖x − y‖. This is norm-dependent segment smoothness, with no global Lipschitz constant assumed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone.lean: spec.valid and segment-bound conjunct of spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is an arbitrary real inner-product space; completeness and finite dimension are not assumed. Public information consists of E, L0, L1, and feasible x0. Hidden budget parameters satisfy R > 0, G ≥ 0, G0 ≥ 0, ε > 0; some VI solution obeys ‖x0 − xstar‖ ≤ R and ‖F(xstar)‖ ≤ G, while ‖F(x0)‖ ≤ G0. X need not be bounded.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and final conjuncts of spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The returned point must belong to X.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the ε residual certificate must hold almost surely under the joint algorithm-seed and oracle-seed probability law.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: The returned point x admits a normal-cone certificate ξ with ⟨ξ, w − x⟩ ≤ 0 for all w ∈ X and ‖F(x) + ξ‖ ≤ ε. The criterion is an unsquared norm residual for F + N_X, rather than a VI gap or the norm of F alone.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The monotone VI formulation and exact projection oracle are established, but norm-dependent segment smoothness, hidden solution-scale bounds, and an almost-sure normal-cone residual guarantee form a meaningful variant of the usual globally Lipschitz VI benchmark.

descriptionHtml:
Constrained Generalized Monotone Inequalities

We consider a variational inequality for a continuous monotone operator F:E→E on a convex set X in a real inner product space E. The operator satisfies a segmentwise generalized Lipschitz condition with constants L0>0 and L1≥0. A given point x0∈X has bounded distance to a solution, with operator norms bounded at both points. Two exact oracles return F(x) and the projection of x onto X. For ε>0, the goal is a feasible output x¯ admitting ξ∈E with ⟨ξ,w−x¯⟩≤0 for every w∈X and ∥F(x¯)+ξ∥≤ε, almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The variational inequality asks for x⋆∈X such that ⟨F(x⋆),w−x⋆⟩≥0for every w∈X. The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The parameters satisfy L0>0,L1≥0,R>0,G≥0,G0≥0,ε>0. The algorithm receives only E, L0, L1, and x0; the parameters R, G, G0, and ε may enter the oracle-call budgets but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convex constraints and projection). The set X⊆E is convex. There exists a map ΠX:E→E satisfying, for every z∈E, ΠX(z)∈X,⟨z−ΠX(z),w−ΠX(z)⟩≤0for every w∈X.

Assumption 2 (Monotonicity and generalized Lipschitz continuity). The operator F is continuous on E and satisfies ⟨F(x)−F(y),x−y⟩≥0for all x,y∈E. For every x,y∈E and M∈R, the segment bound ∥F(x+θ(y−x))∥≤Mfor all θ∈[0,1] implies ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤(L0+L1M)∥x−y∥.

Assumption 3 (Initial point and solution bounds). The given starting point satisfies x0∈X and ∥F(x0)∥≤G0. There exists a solution x⋆ of the variational inequality such that ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,∥F(x⋆)∥≤G.

Queries to either oracle may be made at any point of E. The operator oracle returns F(x) at x, and the projection oracle returns ΠX(z) at z. Calls to these two oracles are counted separately.

For a feasible point x, define its normal cone by NX(x)={ξ∈E:⟨ξ,w−x⟩≤0 for every w∈X}. After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy the normal-cone residual criterion x¯∈X,∃ξ∈NX(x¯):∥F(x¯)+ξ∥≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
In a real inner-product space E, X is convex with an exact projection oracle. The continuous, monotone operator F:E→E satisfies ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤(L0+L1supz∈[x,y]∥F(z)∥)∥x−y∥ for all x,y∈E. Here L0,R,ε>0, L1,G,G0≥0, x0∈X, and there is a VI solution x⋆∈X with ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, ∥F(x⋆)∥≤G, and ∥F(x0)∥≤G0. Target: x∈X and some ξ∈NX(x) with ∥F(x)+ξ∥≤ε, using exact F and projection calls.

Constrained generalized monotone variational inequalities: ConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) ConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O((L0+L1G)(1+L1R)Rε+(1+L1R)2ℓ) total calls; two F calls and one projection per iteration.
(2) PF-NE-EG (Shen and Kılınç-Karzan 2026), App. A, Prop. 2, Lemma 10. Locally Lipschitz F on closed convex X⊆Rd. Derived bound: O(1+R2η∗2ε2+log⁡η0η∗) total F/projection calls, including rejected trials; implicit η∗>0, fixed backtracking factors. (1): ε−1 instead of ε−2 as ε→0 with other parameters fixed; explicit polynomial growth constants, with logarithmic G0 dependence. (1) needs known L0,L1 and global generalized smoothness and monotonicity; (2) needs only local Lipschitz continuity and monotonicity on X.
(3) Composite-EAG (Cai et al. 2024), Thm. 3.2. Special case: globally L-Lipschitz F on Rd, A=NX. O(1+LR/ε) total F/projection calls. (1): Scope extends to operators without a finite global Lipschitz constant. Matches known rate when L1=0 and L=L0. (1) can lose factors 1+L1R and logarithmic overhead for nearly Lipschitz operators; does not cover general proximal inclusions or negative comonotonicity covered by (3).
(4) EG (Choudhury and Loizou 2025), Thm. 3.6. Unconstrained special case: X=E=Rd, G=0. O(1+L02R2ε2+L12R2) F calls. (1): ε−1 instead of ε−2 for fixed remaining parameters and small ε; last instead of best iterate. Scope extends to constraints and F(x⋆)≠0. (1) can lose a logarithmic factor when the L12R2 term dominates (4).
(5) Repository anchored extragradient (LongTails, n.d.). Unconstrained special case: X=E, G=0. O(1+L0Rε+(1+L1R)log(1+(L0+L1G0)Rε)) F calls. (1): Scope extends to constrained VIs with F(x⋆)≠0. (1) loses a factor 1+L1R in the leading term on X=E, and has larger constants.

Abbr: NX(x)={ξ:⟨ξ,w−x⟩≤0 ∀w∈X}; [x,y] is the line segment; ℓ=1+log⁡(1+(L0+L1G0)R/ε). L is a global Lipschitz constant. η0 is the initial step and η∗=inftηt>0 the accepted-step infimum for (2). Total calls sum operator evaluations and projections; projection is the identity when X=E.

source:
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.ProbabilityMeasure
import LongTails.Template

open Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.ConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE

structure Params extends Public where
  R : ℝ
  G : ℝ
  G0 : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  F : p.E → p.E
  X : Set p.E

abbrev spec : Setup where
  numOracles := 2
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ q.L1 ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.G ∧ 0 ≤ q.G0 ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q I oracle :=
    (∀ k seed x, oracle.answer k (0, x) seed = I.F x) ∧
    (∃ P : q.E → q.E, (∀ k seed z, oracle.answer k (1, z) seed = P z) ∧
      ∀ z, P z ∈ I.X ∧ ∀ w ∈ I.X, ⟪z - P z, w - P z⟫ ≤ 0) ∧
    Convex ℝ I.X ∧
    Continuous I.F ∧
    (∀ x y, 0 ≤ ⟪I.F x - I.F y, x - y⟫) ∧
    (∀ x y M, (∀ θ ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ‖I.F (x + θ • (y - x))‖ ≤ M) →
      ‖I.F x - I.F y‖ ≤ (q.L0 + q.L1 * M) * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    q.x0 ∈ I.X ∧
    ‖I.F q.x0‖ ≤ q.G0 ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ I.X, (∀ w ∈ I.X, 0 ≤ ⟪I.F xstar, w - xstar⟫) ∧
      ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R ∧ ‖I.F xstar‖ ≤ q.G)
  successful q I output P :=
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), output ω ∈ I.X ∧
      ∃ ξ : q.E, (∀ w ∈ I.X, ⟪ξ, w - output ω⟫ ≤ 0) ∧ ‖I.F (output ω) + ξ‖ ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.ConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone
